newsitem.title: USA: Talk still thin in sedate U.S. foreign crude scene.
newsitem.headline: Talk still thin in sedate U.S. foreign crude scene.

text.p: Offerings of foreign crudes into the U.S. Gulf Coast remained sparse Tuesday and bids even sparser as the dead zone between July and August delivery programs continued to characterize the market, traders said.

The narrowing spread between North Sea Brent and West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, -- at just $1.05 a barrel as of Tuesday's settlement, helped suppress interest in doing North Sea deals, if not on other grades as well, traders said.
But offers on Latin American grades also remained scarce as players continued to await Ecopetrol's announcement of its August loading program of its light sweet gasoline-rich Cusiana crude oil.
West African blends appeared to be the most widely talked, but even that talk did not render a deal.
A Nigerian Oua Iboe was heard offered at Dated Brent plus $1.85 on an early July delivered basis. Also, two Angolan Cabinda cargoes were heard on offer.
Whatever other offers for delivery into the Gulf Coast in the market were deemed to be a bit too high by some players, who saw the early offers as premature posturing.
One July 6-8 Brent cargo was heard offered at August WTI/Cushing minus 10 cents.

Also BP was said to be floating a preliminary offer for one of its upcoming Cusiana cargoes in August at $1.00 under WTI/Cushing, but other players said they would not likely generate much buying interest until about minus $1.30.

Time will heat up the market according to traders, who say that regardless of the tight Brent-WTI spread, certain U.S. refiners will have to find a way sooner or later, to close deals that their refineries can be fed.
